newsitem.title: UK: Halifax to sell 23 pct of shares at auction.
newsitem.headline: Halifax to sell 23 pct of shares at auction.

text.p: Britain's largest mortgage lender, the Halifax Building Society, said on Tuesday 23 percent of its flotation shares would be sold by members in an initial auction to institutions.
The Halifax plans to float on the London Stock Exchange on June 2.

The Halifax is issuing 2.51 billion shares for its floatation, which will entail a basic handout of 200 shares to members with each package of shares expected to be worth around 1,400 pounds ($2,290).
Of this, 568 million will be sold at the auction, which compares with a figure of almost 27 percent of newly-floated Alliance & Leicester's share allocation to members when it floated in April.
Halifax said that 500 million shares, or 20 percent, will be in the form of a share certificate to members who can then elect to sell their holding in their own time.

Some 49 percent of shares, or 1.23 billion pounds worth, will be held as shareholder accounts. Eight percent of the shares have so far been unclaimed to date, although qualifying members have three years to claim their entitlement.
